title: 1.4 Linear programming: forming inequalities and optimising

q.Q1: Q1. A chair needs 2 hours and a table 4 hours; at most 40 hours are available. They must make at least 4 tables. Write two inequalities.

q.Q2: Q2. For 2x + 4y ≤ 40, find where the boundary line cuts each axis.
q.Q3: Q3. Does the point (0, 0) satisfy 2x + 4y ≤ 40? Which side is wanted?

q.Q4: Q4. The feasible region has vertices (0, 4), (0, 10), (12, 4). Profit P = 500x + 1200y. Find the maximum profit and the mix.

q.Q5: Q5. A farmer has 10 ha for maize (x ha) and beans (y ha). Maize needs KSh 3000/ha and beans KSh 6000/ha; the budget is KSh 48 000. Write both constraints.
q.Q6: Q6. Why does the optimum always occur at a vertex?

q.Q7: Q7. For the farmer, with x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0, the vertices are (0, 0), (10, 0), (4, 6) and (0, 8). Profit is KSh 20 000/ha for maize and KSh 35 000/ha for beans. Find the best plan.
